candidate.answerReason: Both runners complete 5/(2π) laps per minute. Their opposite-direction progress totals 5/π laps per minute, so passes occur at kπ/5 minutes for positive integers k. Exactly k=1 through 47 occur within 30 minutes.

methods.label: Compare progress in laps
methods.explanation:
The lanes have different lengths, so compare laps per minute. Because the runners occupy different lanes, a pass means being side by side on the same ray from the center.

The inner and outer circumferences are \(100\pi\) and \(120\pi\) meters. Their lap rates are therefore
\[
\frac{250}{100\pi}=\frac{5}{2\pi},
\qquad
\frac{300}{120\pi}=\frac{5}{2\pi}.
\]
Since they run in opposite directions from the same ray, they are side by side exactly when their combined progress makes a whole number of laps. Their combined rate is \(5/\pi\) laps per minute, so the \(k\)th pass after the start occurs at
\[
t_k=\frac{k\pi}{5}\text{ minutes},
\qquad k=1,2,3,\ldots.
\]
Using \(3.14<\pi<3.15\), we obtain \(47\pi<150<48\pi\). Consequently,
\[
\frac{47\pi}{5}<30<\frac{48\pi}{5}.
\]
Thus passes 1 through 47 occur during the run, while pass 48 occurs afterward. The initial alignment corresponds to \(k=0\) and is excluded. The answer is \(\boxed{47}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
